relevance_note: One cohort member carries a TNFAIP3 deletion: "A monoallelic loss of TNFAIP3 was caused by a heterozygous 59.9 kb deletion in patient-191".
method_note: Read the full Markdown by hand; a short script only assembled and checked the JSON (spans verified verbatim, all schema fields present). Scope: this is a 191-patient CNV study of suspected inborn errors of immunity; only patient-191 has a TNFAIP3 variant, so only patient-191 is extracted. The other 19 CNV carriers named in the text (patient-005, -060, -063, -047, -141, -008, -017, -180, -058, -122, -081, -083, -074, -090, -171, -160, -149, -094, -114) carry variants in other genes or loci, none in TNFAIP3, and were deliberately not extracted. Table 1 (per-patient CNV/SNV details, presumably including sex, age, clinical diagnosis and coordinates) has only its caption and notes in the Markdown; its body and the supplement (Table S1) are absent, so sex, ages, clinical diagnosis, genomic coordinates and breakpoints for patient-191 are recorded as not reported. No SNV is reported for patient-191 (the SNV paragraph names only patient-063, -094, -074, -171 and -083); this silence is not recorded as a negative finding. 'the carrier' in the clinical-manifestations sentence refers to patient-191 named two sentences earlier, so the five features are recorded as stated for this individual. Checklist 'skin lesions' is marked observed on the basis of rosacea (judgement call); chronic sinusitis is not treated as 'recurrent infections' and pulmonary emphysema not as interstitial lung disease (both left not reported). The paper links the deletion to A20 haploinsufficiency only generically ('haploinsufficiency of A20 has been described to cause autoinflammatory disease'), so disease_label_as_stated is not reported. cites_prior_report_of_same_patients is true only because patient-005 (ICOS) was previously reported (ref. 23); nothing says patient-191 was reported before. The parental-testing statement is a study-wide limitation, not specific to patient-191; inheritance is not reported. Contradictions in the paper (none involving TNFAIP3): the patient-180 22q11.2 deletion is '740.0 kb' in Results but '704 kb' in Discussion; the PIK3R1 variant is cited as 'MIM 171,833#0008' in Results and 'MIM 616,005#0008' in Discussion; the patient-074 duplication is described as a '739 kb TD including CORO1A' in Results and a 'TD of 576 kb' (16p11.2) in Discussion.

study_type.span: We identified a total of 20 CNVs using whole exome sequencing data of a cohort of 191 patients with a suspected IEI.

n_patients_reported.span: A monoallelic loss of TNFAIP3 was caused by a heterozygous 59.9 kb deletion in patient-191 (Fig. 1b).
